clue.text: Donor's complaint about new player

indicators.note: a complaint wrapped about something holds it inside, so the next piece goes within

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or complaint
an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: A donor grumbles about a newcomer to the cast or team.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Donor stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person who gives money or help to a cause is a donor.

clue.text: Have a punt on other side

definitions.meaning: to bet on a horse or team, punt being British slang for a wager
the reverse or rear face of something

explanation.surface: A gambler weighs betting on the opposing team.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: supporting with a stake, and the rear of an object, as in the reverse of a page.

clue.text: Contracts speeded up arguments

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the preceding word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ran is to have speeded along
rows are noisy quarrels

explanation.surface: Deals got rushed through after heated disputes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracts' looks like a noun for deals but is the verb meaning gets smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: something that contracts becomes tighter or less wide.

clue.text: Criminal soon vilified by female's spatial perception

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are twisted or crooked, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer is quickly denounced by a woman with a keen eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like the subject of the sentence but signals rearranging 'soon vilified'; 'by' joins the female letter to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the whole area a person can see at once is their visual range, a sense of space.

clue.text: Furniture item requiring copper lead on a rod, possibly

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

indicators.note: possibly hints the letters given could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Fitting a piece of furniture needs a metal rod, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requiring' and 'on' are joining words; 'copper' and 'lead' are both chemical symbols, not police or leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cabinet with shelves and doors is a classic household piece of furniture.

clue.text: Evenly poached — ain't much water

indicators.note: evenly tells us to take the letters in even positions only

explanation.surface: A cook complains that poaching doesn't use a lot of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a sea covering a vast area holds an enormous quantity of water.

clue.text: Responsibility, having advantage but losing the lead

indicators.note: losing the lead means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a bonus is an extra benefit or advantage

explanation.surface: A team bears the burden, holding an edge but then falling behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a burden or duty that falls on someone is their responsibility.

clue.text: Robin circulates around first-class capital

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the next piece, holding it inside
circulates suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A robin flies around a top-notch city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Robin' looks like the bird doing the circling, but 'circulates' scrambles its letters into N...ROBI, which go 'around' A1, the top grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this city is the capital of Kenya.

clue.text: He nicks your stuff if he's taken amiss

indicators.note: amiss means wrongly placed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man steals your things if he gets the wrong idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a petty thief who slips in unseen to steal; nick is British slang for steal.

clue.text: Feel concern about victory appearing in court division

indicators.note: one word going about another surrounds it

parts.note: to care is to feel concern
V for victory is a common abbreviation
up before the court, up means appearing in court

explanation.surface: Someone worries about winning a case before a divided court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing' is a joining word; 'court division' looks like one idea, but 'court' belongs with 'in' to give UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a carve-up is a sharing-out of spoils, a division between parties.

clue.text: Inflammatory European rationale

parts.note: a motive is the reason behind an action

explanation.surface: A provocative European explains their reasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: language that stirs strong feelings is inflammatory.

clue.text: Apparently where hands must work round the clock …

definitions.text: where hands must work round the clock
definitions.meaning: the hands of a clock move around its dial

explanation.surface: Workers seem to be put on twenty-four-hour shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next one; 'hands' are not workers but a clock's pointers.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom meaning judging by surface appearances; literally, clock hands sweep across the dial.

clue.text: Nobody let off Labour association

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: labour means work

explanation.surface: No one was released from a trade-union link with the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' with its capital looks like the political party but just means work.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an informal network of former schoolmates helping each other, an association of privilege.

clue.text: … then, behind parts of hospital

parts.note: after means behind in order or time
wards are the sections of a hospital

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, then, at the back of the hospital units.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: later on, subsequently, at a later time.

clue.text: Quiet footballers in company providing breeding ground for schools

indicators.note: the pieces sit in the company word, inside it

parts.note: a firm is a business company
sh is the call for quiet
the FA is the Football Association, governing English football

explanation.surface: Silent players in a club that nurtures youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'schools' are not classrooms but groups of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a place where fish, which swim in schools, are bred and raised.

clue.text: Frozen? It helps to cover top

indicators.note: the words cover the answer, which lies concealed within them

explanation.surface: If something is frozen, it helps to put a lid on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the highest point or peak of something.

clue.text: Stick out rubbish hoarded by strait-laced type

indicators.note: something hoarded by a person is held within them

parts.note: a prude is a priggish, strait-laced person
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A puritan keeps their junk and refuses to throw it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to jut or project beyond a surface.

clue.text: Listen in rage, lost, crossing central London district

indicators.note: the shuffled letters cross over and hold the next piece inside
lost suggests the letters have gone astray, so they are rearranged

parts.note: W1 is the postcode for central London's West End, the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: An eavesdropper loses their temper going through the West End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' scrambles the temper into E...ARG, 'crossing' it over the district; the London postcode W1 covers the West End, its 1 doubling as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to eavesdrop on others' conversation.

clue.text: Summarised article pinched by hobo

indicators.note: something pinched by a person is held tight inside them

parts.note: a rover is a wanderer or tramp
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A report on an item stolen by a tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to go through something briefly, as in recapping notes before a talk.

clue.text: Heart, perhaps, is initially eager and direct

parts.note: the heart is an example of a bodily organ

indicators.note: initially means take just the first letter

explanation.surface: The heart, maybe, is keen and straightforward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'direct' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to arrange or manage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to arrange and manage an event or group.

clue.text: Annoying a few, supporting church with no roof

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporter goes below what it holds up
in a down clue, no roof means the top letter is removed

parts.note: kirk is the Scottish word for church
some means a few

explanation.surface: A few people propping up a roofless church find it a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tiresome, causing irritation.

clue.text: Successful run of king after life (metaphorically) in turbulent water

indicators.note: the king piece comes after the rest
the life word sits in the churned water
turbulent water is churned up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an innings, a cricket batsman's turn, is a metaphor for a lifetime
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A long-lived monarch rides out choppy seas on a lucky run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' gives W...TREA; in cricket a batsman's innings is their spell at the crease, a common metaphor for a lifespan ('a good innings').
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a series of consecutive victories is a successful run.

clue.text: Harvest acres within valley

indicators.note: the acres letter goes within the valley word

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland
A is the abbreviation for acres

explanation.surface: A farmer gathers crops from fields in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to gather crops left over after the main reaping.

clue.text: Go around with no end of paper for sketch

indicators.note: with no means the following letter is taken away

parts.note: to skirt something is to go around its edge

indicators.note: end of means the last letter

explanation.surface: An artist walks round with no paper left for drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sketch' looks like a drawing but means a short comic piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a short comic sketch performed on stage or on television.

clue.text: Income generated by engineers replacing start of tree-lined road

indicators.note: one piece takes the place of the first letter of another

parts.note: an avenue is a broad road often lined with trees
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Money made by engineers rebuilding a leafy boulevard.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: money coming in, especially to a government or company.

clue.text: Ruin fun and stagger, showing force out of habit

indicators.note: to ruin is to wreck, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: to rock is to sway or stagger

explanation.surface: A killjoy spoils the fun and totters, breaking a routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' is not a custom but a monk's or nun's robe.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: to expel a priest from holy orders, literally stripping their robe.

clue.text: Type like this vacuous recruit

parts.note: so means in this way

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so only the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: A kind of empty-headed new soldier, like this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a kind, class or variety.

clue.text: Popular item of underwear intended, reportedly, for capital

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a vest is a British undershirt

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so this piece sounds like a word

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A fashionable undershirt bought, they say, for the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city but means money put to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: money committed to a venture for profit is capital.
